subject: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + KMS residency / crypto provenance
messages:
From: Susan Patel <susan.patel@acuitymed.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AcuityMed InfoSec <security@acuitymed.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + KMS residency / crypto provenance

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As part of our final security review ahead of procurement, we need a consolidated subprocessor roster that includes:

- Current active subprocessors (name + service provided + region of data processing)
- Whether each subprocessor has access to encrypted data at rest or keys (yes/no)
- KMS key custody model for any subprocessor that handles keys (Redwood-managed HSM, customer-managed KMS, third-party custodial)
- Residency / data flow map for any subprocessor that performs inference or stores logs

Can you also provide a short provenance note describing cryptographic controls in place (e.g., KMS rotation cadence, key wrapping practices) and the most recent SOC 2 snapshot and CAIQ section references if available? We are aiming to close the vendor sign-off by EOD May 3.

Attachments are fine — a simple CSV + an annotated spreadsheet for KMS mapping would work. If you have a short attestation that covers key custody and residency, that will speed things up.

Appreciate it — feel free to loop in whoever owns infra/security on your side.

Best,
Susan
Susan Patel
Sr. InfoSec Manager, AcuityMed
security@acuitymed.com

[attachment: purchase_order_template.docx (referenced, not required)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Susan Patel <susan.patel@acuitymed.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:03:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + KMS residency / crypto provenance

Susan — thanks for the detailed ask. Looping in Jonas (security lead, supply chain) and Ben (platform infra) to pull the artifacts.

Planned deliverables (we can hit your May 3 date):
- A CSV listing subprocessors with columns: name, service, region(s), has_data_access (Y/N), has_key_access (Y/N), key_custody_model, comments
- KMS residency matrix (Excel) with key ownership, wrapping, rotation cadence, and HSM provider where relevant
- SOC 2 snapshot PDF and pointers to CAIQ sections (we'll annotate the relevant rows)
- A one-paragraph attestation on key custody and residency for signature

Ben / Jonas — can you confirm the current subprocessor export and whether we have a short attestation template? If helpful I can draft the attestation and run it by legal.

Susan — we'll aim to send the files by EOD Wed (Apr 28) so you have time to review ahead of your internal close. If you need anything earlier, tell us which pieces are highest priority.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

[internal note: we'll include the export and a separate KMS mapping excel; attach SOC2 snapshot from our evidence repo]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 13:15:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + KMS residency / crypto provenance

Folks — attaching the export and KMS matrix as discussed. Highlights:

- Attached CSV (redwood_subprocessors_20270427.csv): includes 42 active subprocessors. Fields populated for region and has_key_access. We flagged 5 providers with potential key access (inference pools + metrics aggregator).
- KMS_residency_matrix_20270427.xlsx: shows which keys are Redwood-managed (AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys), customer-managed (rare, only in Private deployments), and third-party custodial (we use a partner for archival keys in APAC).
- SOC2_snapshot_202612.pdf: redacted evidence bundle (control mapping) — note this is the latest public snapshot we can share.

Open items for attestation: Jonas — can you draft the one-paragraph statement on rotation cadence and wrapping? I can include a short line referencing the APAC archival custodial provider and their residency.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20270427.csv (CSV stub), kms_residency_matrix_20270427.xlsx (xlsx stub), SOC2_snapshot_202612.pdf (PDF stub)

-Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Security, Redwood Inference

[Quoted for context]
On Tue, Apr 27, 2027 at 10:03 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Susan — thanks for the detailed ask. Looping in Jonas (security lead, supply chain) and Ben (platform infra) to pull the artifacts.

> - A CSV listing subprocessors...

From: Susan Patel <susan.patel@acuitymed.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AcuityMed InfoSec <security@acuitymed.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Apr 2027 08:02:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated subprocessor roster + KMS residency / crypto provenance

Lauren / Ben / Jonas — thank you, this is very helpful and the level of detail is exactly what we needed. A couple of quick follow-ups:

1) Can you add the ISO country code for each subprocessor processing location in the CSV? That will speed our data residency mapping.
2) For the five flagged providers with key access, could you indicate whether they have access to unencrypted logs or only to encrypted blobs (and under which role)?
3) We need a signed attestation for key custody and data residency. Could you send a DocuSign link or similar (see related_links) so our procurement team can accept it formally?

If you can deliver the updated CSV + the one-paragraph attestation by EOD Tue May 3, we can move forward on PO.

Best,
Susan
Sr. InfoSec Manager, AcuityMed

[attachment: procurement_checklist.pdf - referenced]
